files.lesson.md: --- order: 2 unit: area node: AC9M7M01 n1 title: Area of triangles summary: "Two copies of any triangle, one turned round, make a parallelogram with the same base and height. So a triangle's area is half of base × height: A = ½bh." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Sails, roof gables and the slices of a pizza cut into wedges are triangles. How much fabric does a triangular sail need?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8274 url: http://127.0.0.1:8274/index.html readySelector: "#sl-s" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: area.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A turned copy (dashed) makes a parallelogram, $6 \\times 4 = 24$ cm². The triangle is half: $\\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 6 \\times 4 = 12$ cm²." } explainClip: query: { code: "@area.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Half a parallelogram" say: "A triangle is half of a parallelogram." clip: - caption: { text: "Add a turned copy of the triangle.", say: "Add a copy of the triangle, turned round." } - click: Add a turned copy - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 12" } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "Together: a parallelogram, 6 × 4 = 24. The triangle is half: 12.", say: "Together they make a parallelogram. The triangle is half of it." } - wait: 1400 - click: Remove the copy - caption: { text: "Move the top: same base, same height, same area.", say: "Move the top along. The area stays the same." } - click: Move the top right - click: Move the top right - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 12" } - wait: 1000 --- A triangle also has a **base** (any side) and a **perpendicular height**: the distance from the opposite corner (the apex) straight down to the base, at a right angle. ## Predict: a 6 by 4 triangle ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an area for a triangle with base 6 and height 4 shows whether they halve, or multiply as for a parallelogram." check: type: predict q: "A triangle has base 6 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. What is its area?" options: ["12 cm²", "24 cm²", "10 cm²", "20 cm²"] actual: "12 cm². Two copies make a 6 by 4 parallelogram, 24 cm², so one triangle is half: 12 cm². 24 is the parallelogram." ``` How would two copies of the triangle fit together? ## Run: add a turned copy ```step stage: run insight: "Adding a turned copy shows two triangles make a parallelogram with the same base and height, so the triangle is half; moving the apex keeps the area." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#run", height: 540 } check: { type: board, text: "Press **Add a turned copy**. What do the two triangles make? Then move the top along. Was your prediction right?", when: "c = 1", explain: "A parallelogram with base 6 and height 4, area 24 cm², so the triangle is half: 12 cm². Moving the top keeps the base and height, so the area stays 12." } ``` The dashed orange line is the height, from the top straight down to the base. Here's why the turned copy gives the area. Two copies of a triangle, one turned round, fit together into a parallelogram with the same base and height. So the triangle is **half** of it: $$A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times b \times h$$ ## Investigate: half of base times height ```step stage: investigate insight: "A = ½bh; Omar forgets the half, giving the parallelogram. The height can fall outside the triangle, onto the base extended." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "A triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. What is its area, in cm²?" answer: "35" feedback: - ["70", "That is the parallelogram two copies make. The triangle is half."] - ["17", "That adds. Multiply, then halve."] explain: "½ × 10 × 7 = 35 cm²." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#omar" text: "Omar finds the area of a triangle. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: triangle-no-half explain: "Line 2: a triangle is half of base × height. ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm²." - picture: { ref: area.yml#obtuse-pic, caption: "A triangle with base 4 cm whose top leans past the end of the base." } check: type: question q: "Where is this triangle's perpendicular height?" options: ["Outside the triangle: straight down from the top to the base, extended", "Along the longest side", "It has no height, because the top is not above the base"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The longest side slants. The height meets the base line at a right angle.", "Every triangle has a height: extend the base until the line from the top meets it."] explain: "Extend the base (dashed) and drop the height from the top at a right angle. The area is still ½ × 4 × 4 = 8 cm²." ``` ### Halve it Here is the reason, then the routine. ```worked 6 \times 4 = 24 :: Two copies of the triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height. A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12 \text{ cm}^2 :: One triangle is half of it. A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 7 = 35 \text{ cm}^2 :: Multiply the base by the height, then halve (or halve first: 5 × 7). ``` Now try one: base 10 cm, height 7 cm. ### Find the mistake Read Omar's working. What shape has area base × height? ### A height outside ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a height outside the triangle on the board, building an area from a base, a new triangle, a missing height (backwards), then a right-angled triangle where the height is a side." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#outside", height: 540 } tasks: - starter: "area.yml#outside" hint: "Move the top past either end of the base." check: { type: board, text: "Move the top so the height falls outside the triangle. Does the area change?", when: "o = 1", explain: "The base is extended (dashed) to meet the height. Still ½ × 4 × 4 = 8 cm²." } - starter: "area.yml#twelve" hint: ["½ × 4 × h = 12, so 4 × h = 24.", "Set b to 4 first."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a triangle with base 4 cm and area 12 cm².", when: "b = 4 and a = 12", explain: "½ × 4 × 6 = 12: the height is 6 cm." } - check: type: answer q: "Base 9 cm, perpendicular height 4 cm. Area, in cm²?" answer: "18" feedback: - ["36", "Halve it: a triangle is half the parallelogram."] explain: "½ × 9 × 4 = 18 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "A triangle has area 20 cm² and base 8 cm. What is its perpendicular height, in cm?" answer: "5" feedback: - ["2.5", "That uses base × height = 20. For a triangle, ½ × 8 × h = 20, so 8 × h = 40."] - ["80", "That multiplies. Undo the steps: double 20, then divide by 8."] explain: "½ × 8 × h = 20, so 4 × h = 20 and h = 5 cm." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Two copies of this triangle, area 20 cm² each, fit together into a parallelogram. What is the parallelogram's area, in cm²?", answer: 40, tolerance: 0, explain: "20 + 20 = 40 cm². Its base is 8 cm, so what height gives 40?" } - check: type: question q: "Edge case: a right-angled triangle has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm, with the right angle between the 6 cm and 8 cm sides. What is its area?" options: ["24 cm²", "48 cm²", "30 cm²", "40 cm²"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Halve it.", "10 cm is the sloping side. Use the two sides at the right angle.", "10 cm is the sloping side. Use the two sides at the right angle."] explain: "The two sides at the right angle are a base and its height: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm²." ``` ### A height outside Each task changes one thing. ### Area 12 ### Another triangle ### Backwards: the height ### A right angle ## Practise: triangles ```step stage: practise insight: "Whole and decimal answers and half a rectangle, mixed; forgetting the half is the planted slip; the review keeps parallelograms fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Base 12 m, perpendicular height 5 m. Area, in m²?" answer: "30" feedback: - ["60", "Halve it."] explain: "½ × 12 × 5 = 30 m²." - check: type: answer q: "Base 7 cm, perpendicular height 3 cm. Area, in cm²?" answer: "10.5" feedback: - ["21", "Halve it."] - ["10", "Half of 21 is 10.5."] explain: "½ × 7 × 3 = 10.5 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "A 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle is cut along a diagonal. What is the area of one triangle, in cm²?" answer: "30" feedback: - ["60", "That is the whole rectangle."] explain: "Half of 10 × 6 = 60: 30 cm²." - check: type: answer q: "Review: a parallelogram has base 7 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Area, in cm²?" answer: "42" feedback: - ["21", "A parallelogram is not halved: only a triangle is."] explain: "7 × 6 = 42 cm²." ``` ### Halve it ### A decimal answer ### Half a rectangle ### Review: parallelograms ## Make: area 15 ```step stage: make insight: "Building a triangle with a given area means choosing a base and height whose product is double it." try: { playground: board, starter: "area.yml#make", height: 560 } hint: ["½ × b × h = 15, so b × h = 30.", "Which pairs multiply to 30 and fit the sliders?"] check: { type: board, text: "Make a triangle with area 15 cm².", when: "a = 15", explain: "b × h must be 30: base 6 and height 5, base 10 and height 3, or base 5 and height 6." } ``` Then find a second triangle with the same area and a different base. ## Make: a sail, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A sailmaker's cloth is the sail's area: base along the boom, perpendicular height up the mast, then halve." hint: ["Which two sides meet at a right angle?", "A triangle is half of base × height."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A triangular sail has a base of 3.2 m along the boom and a perpendicular height of 5 m up the mast. How much cloth does it need, in m², not counting the seams?" steps: - ["The boom and mast meet at a right angle, so the base is 3.2 m and the height is 5 m", "the height is perpendicular to the base"] - ["$A = \\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 3.2 \\times 5$", "a triangle is half of base × height"] - ["$A = \\tfrac{1}{2} \\times 16 = 8$ m²", "multiply, then halve"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is there a half in the working?" options: - "Two copies of the triangle make a parallelogram of base × height, so one triangle is half" - "A sail has two sides, so you halve" - "The height is only half as long as it looks" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A sail is flat cloth in one piece here. The half comes from the shape.", "The height is the whole 5 m. The half is for the triangle, not for the height."] answer: "8" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["16", "That is base × height, the parallelogram. A triangle is half of it."] - ["8.2", "That adds the two lengths. Multiply, then halve."] criteria: - "I sketched the sail and marked the base and the perpendicular height." - "I halved base × height." - "My answer is in m²." explain: "3.2 × 5 = 16 and half of 16 is 8, so the sail needs 8 m² of cloth." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The sail's measurements are made up for the task; a real sail has curved edges. Sketch it, mark the base and the height, and type the area. **Also used in** - **Sails.** A sailmaker orders cloth by the sail's area, from its base and height. - **Gable ends.** A painter quoting for the triangular end of a house works out its area first, then the litres of paint. ```teacher summary: Students double a triangle with a turned copy to make a parallelogram, see why A = ½bh, find heights that fall outside obtuse triangles, and work backwards from an area (AC9M7M01, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can explain why a triangle's area is half of base × height. - I can find the area of any triangle, including one whose height falls outside it. - I can find a missing base or height from an area. struggle: Working backwards from an area to a height (doubling before dividing). Ask students to write ½ × 8 × h = 20 and undo one step at a time, rather than giving them the rule. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the parallelogram area (previous lesson). The one idea: two copies of a triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height, so the triangle is half. The common mistake is forgetting the half (Omar's mistake). Obtuse triangles have a height outside the shape, onto the base extended. running: - "Predict: students who chose 24 found the parallelogram." - "Run: ask what shape the two copies make, and why it has the same height." - "Investigate: on the obtuse picture, ask students to trace the height from the top to the dashed extension." - "Modify: for the right-angled triangle, ask which two sides are at the right angle." - "Make: collect base and height pairs; all multiply to 30." - "Paper: the sail is worked in books. Books out; look for the sketch with the height marked at a right angle to the boom, and the half." stuck: - see: A student forgets to halve (Omar's mistake). ask: What shape has area base × height? fix: Two triangles make that parallelogram; one triangle is half. - see: A student says an obtuse triangle has no height. ask: Where would a plumb line from the top land? fix: Extend the base; the height meets it at a right angle. - see: A student uses the sloping side of a right-angled triangle. ask: Which two sides meet at the right angle? fix: Those two are a base and its height. stretch: Draw four different triangles on squared paper with area 12 cm², including one with its height outside. support: Use the board for every triangle, and cut paper triangles in half pairs. leads: > Next: Area problems (node 2): choosing the base and height, units, and shapes made of rectangles and triangles. Where it leads: area of trapeziums (Year 8), and the cross-section of triangular prisms (Volume). exit: q: "A triangle has base 9 cm and height 6 cm. Find its area. A triangle with area 24 cm² has base 8 cm: find its height." a: ½ × 9 × 6 = 27 cm². ½ × 8 × h = 24, so h = 6 cm. explain: > Two copies of a triangle, one turned round, make a parallelogram with the same base and height. So the triangle's area is **half** of base × height: $$A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times b \times h$$ The height is perpendicular to the base. If the top leans past the end of the base, extend the base: the height meets it outside the triangle. Moving the top along a line parallel to the base keeps the area. ```
